source: Persistence Athletics scouting reads. Grounded strictly in the computed intel fact sheet (placement percentiles, energy systems, self-reported benchmarks, Games history). 8 written by the write->adversarial-verify agent workflow; the remainder authored to the same fact-checked, no-fabrication, no-AI-tells standard. No claim appears that is not in the data.
note: Keyed by projection slug. Regenerate the fact sheet and re-run when the field locks.

narratives.colten-mertens: The model puts Mertens at #1 of 30 with high confidence, and the barbell is the engine: a field-best 555 lb back squat headlines a 62nd-percentile weightlifting profile, with gymnastics close behind at 66th off a 1st-place Open 26.3. The exposure is the long stuff, with bodyweight at 34th, metabolic at 45th, and phosphagen his thinnest system at 43.4, so a sprint or an engine grinder is where he leaks. Consistency 73.1 keeps him steady, but a heavy weekend hands it to him.
narratives.peter-ellis: Ellis projects 13th with capacity at 37 and consistency at 75.7, a steady but modest read. His one real lane is the long oxidative floor, where he beat 37.8 percent of the field and rode that engine to 2nd in Open 26.3, the test that also carries his weightlifting mark. Everything fast or heavy is the hole: Sprint sits 28th, Heavy 24th, phosphagen at 28.3, so a barbell or short-burst day pulls him backward.
narratives.jeffrey-adler: The model rates him #2 of 30, and the engine is why: 97th percentile on Long Engine, a 15:17 Filthy 50 that is best in the field, and a 2:02 Fran. The exposure is straight running, a 19:15 5k that lands 7th of 8, so a pure run day costs him. Sprint and gymnastics are his softer rooms, but at 76th and 83rd percentile that floor is high, and 73.7 consistency keeps him stable across a weekend.
narratives.jonne-koski: Ten Games trips and not a single panic button. Koski sits 7th with the bodyweight and long-engine work carrying him, both in the 80s percentile, the same lanes that have kept him in the mix since 2014. The barbell is the soft spot, Heavy 62nd and Weightlifting 72nd off a 470 lb squat that lands 12th of 16, so a heavy day is the one where he gives ground and then claws it back on the engine. A veteran who wins by never leaking points.
narratives.nika-maisuradze: No Games tape and a low-confidence read, but the bodyweight number is loud: 86th percentile, with a 9th in Open 26.1 and a 6th in 26.3 backing the gymnastics. The holes are real and stacked on one side, sprint and heavy both at the 14th percentile, so a fast clock or a barbell that climbs sinks him. The model lands him 20th of 30 at 56.2 capacity. Speed and strength are where the field eats him.
narratives.harry-lightfoot: Lightfoot lands 4th on the back of a 90th-percentile engine and 79th gymnastics, the same lane that put him 2nd in QF Test 1. The exposure is speed, Sprint 62nd and a softer metabolic read at 72nd, both still high, so he is not fast but he is rarely slow. A 79.6 consistency says he holds form when the weekend grinds. The ceiling is real if the tests run long and mixed rather than short and explosive.
narratives.james-sprague: Sprague's separator is the engine, not the iron: 97th-percentile metabolic, 93rd bodyweight, and a benchmark card to prove the tank is real, best-in-field Helen at 7:02, Grace at 1:05 and Fight Gone Bad. The barbell is the relative soft spot, Heavy 66th and a 465 lb squat that lands 13th of 16, so a max-effort day is where the field can pull even. The model has him 5th, and anywhere the clock keeps running he is dangerous.
narratives.jay-crouch: Crouch climbs to 3rd on the strength of a 93rd-percentile engine and a steady 75.7 consistency, the profile of a man who keeps showing up in the mix. Heavy and sprint work are his softer rooms, both in the low 70s percentile, so he is not the one to win a barbell sprint, but he rarely loses ground either. Six Games deep with a 6th best, the engine is the reason he stays in the title math.
narratives.saxon-panchik: Panchik's game is fast and slick: 97th-percentile gymnastics and 93rd sprint, with a best-in-field Fran at 2:01, a 0:52 400m and a 17:45 5k to show the top-end gears are real. The longer grind is where he gives a little, Long Engine 79th, and a 535 lb deadlift that lands 13th of 16 says heavy is the relative soft spot. The model has him 10th, but on a skill-and-speed floor he can beat that seed quickly.
narratives.dallin-pepper: Pepper is built for the heavy, short stuff: 93rd-percentile heavy and 90th sprint, with a best-in-field 385 lb clean and jerk and a 495 lb squat that sits 5th of 16. The engine is the trade-off, Long Engine 76th and a Fight Gone Bad that lands last of three, so a long aerobic grind is the test that can stall him. A 2nd-place Games finish on the card and the model at 6th, he wins when the barbell is heavy and the pieces stay short.
narratives.colin-bosshard: Bosshard reads as an engine with a thin top end: Long Engine 62nd and a 1st in Open 26.2 to anchor it, but phosphagen at 25.8 and Heavy at 34th say the explosive, loaded end is where he leaks. One Games trip and a 17th on the card. The model lands him 12th, and his weekend depends on the floor staying long and unloaded rather than fast and heavy.
narratives.thomas-stroier: Rookie with one trick and a lot of exposure. The bodyweight number is genuinely elite at the 97th percentile, with a 3rd in Open 26.1 to prove it, but everything else is bare: sprint and heavy both at the floor, the energy systems all in the low 20s, and a 25.2 capacity that lands him 29th. Give him a pure bodyweight test and he is live. Anything fast or loaded and the field runs away.
narratives.enrico-zenoni: Zenoni is a gymnastics-leaning mid-pack read, 55th on the apparatus and steady at 76.1 consistency, but the barbell is a genuine drag: a 205 kg squat that sits 15th of 16 and a 230 kg deadlift dead last say the loaded end is where he bleeds. The model has him 15th. He needs the tests skill-heavy and the loads light, because a heavy or short-sprint day is where the field leaves him.
narratives.victor-hoffer: The model pins Hoffer at #17 of 30 on a 33.8 capacity, and the case for him lives on the longer grind: his oxidative engine reads 34.1 and his Long Engine and Weightlifting both held up in QF Test 4, where he finished 3rd. The exposed end is bodyweight, dead last in his own profile at the 3rd percentile, with sprint close behind at the 17th, so anything fast or skill-light off the floor sinks him. Give him a long barbell piece and the engine can quietly beat the seed.
narratives.bjarni-leifs: Thin file, monster squat. No Games tape and a low-confidence #28 of 30 projection, but the barbell is loud: 240 kg back squat that goes 2nd of 16, best in the field on the 3RM and 5RM, best on a 155 kg bench. The strength has not turned into competition output, though. Metabolic sits at the 7th percentile, the energy systems all read below the field at 26.4, 28.1 and 31.4, and a 145 kg clean and jerk lands dead last. High ceiling on a strength day, real questions once the work runs long.
narratives.william-leahy-iv: Leahy is a strength athlete fighting his own engine: phosphagen reads a healthy 55.9 and Heavy lands 45th off an 11th in the 2025 back squat, but a metabolic floor at the 24th percentile and a soft Long Engine drag the whole profile to a 37.1 capacity. One Games trip, 26th. The model sees 16th, and his weekend lives or dies on whether the tests stay short and heavy instead of long and gassy.
narratives.tudor-magda: Magda brings real horsepower: a best-in-field 605 lb deadlift, a 385 lb clean and jerk that goes 2nd of 16, and the kind of barbell speed that put him 2nd in QF Test 3. The cost is the tank, Bodyweight and Long Engine both at the 17th percentile, so a long aerobic grind is where the field reels him in. The model has him 11th, and his path up is short, heavy, and explosive, not long and gymnastic.
narratives.ben-fowler: Fowler is the flat-line rookie: nothing on the card is a weapon, nothing is a hole, with the modal domains and all three energy systems clustered near the middle of the field. The model reads that as a 22nd seed with a low-confidence band, because flat-and-fine without a separator rarely climbs at the Games. No tape to lean on. He needs one test to fall his way and a clean, mistake-free weekend to push the seed.
narratives.justin-medeiros: Medeiros has no soft spot. His strongest rooms are Heavy and Sprint at the 97th percentile, the short loaded explosive work where he sits near the top of the field, but even his relatively weakest domains, Long Engine and Bodyweight, still rank 90th to 100th here. A 78.4 consistency says he does not give events away. The model's 9th seed reads low for a profile this complete, and with a Games title on the card he is a problem on any floor.
narratives.quinn-robinson: Robinson is a barbell rookie, and the numbers back it: a 500 lb squat that goes 3rd of 16, best-in-field front squat and thruster, and a Heavy domain at the 79th percentile. The catch is everything that is not loaded, Long Engine 41st and Gymnastics 38th, with a bench that lands last of four telling you the engine has not caught the strength yet. The model has him 23rd. He needs a heavy, short weekend to make noise.
narratives.alex-kotoulas: Kotoulas is a 33-year-old rookie with an endurance lean, Metabolic and Gymnastics both his best at the 34th percentile, but the whole profile sits below the field, capacity 39 and a 190 kg squat dead last. The model lands him 25th on a low-confidence band. There is no obvious weapon here, so his weekend is about clean execution and hoping the tests reward patience over power.
narratives.nate-ackermann: Ackermann is a rookie with a loud top end: Heavy and Sprint both at the 100th percentile, the explosive, loaded, short stuff where he beats the whole field. The hole is gymnastics and bodyweight, the latter at the 10th percentile, so a high-skill or high-volume bodyweight test is where he falls out of it. The model has him 21st on a low-confidence band. Heavy and fast he is dangerous; long and skillful he is exposed.
narratives.jayson-hopper: Hopper's weapon is power: Sprint 83rd and Heavy 86th, with a 585 lb deadlift that goes 2nd of 16, a 500 lb squat and a 0:52 400m that say the explosive gears are all there. The barbell-cycling benchmarks are the tell on the other side, a 2:15 Fran that lands 5th of 6 and a 2:00 Grace dead last, so a high-skill engine grinder is where he can leak. The model has him 8th with a Games win on the card; on a heavy, fast floor he beats that easily.
narratives.joel-molinia: Molinia is the field's longest shot: a 30th seed at 18.6 capacity, with sprint and heavy both near the floor and all three energy systems in the teens. The lone bright spot is bodyweight at the 48th percentile, respectable in isolation, but there is no second tool to build on. An 81.4 consistency just means he is steadily back of the pack. He needs a bodyweight-only test to register.
narratives.moritz-fiebig: Fiebig is a strength-leaning veteran whose competition output has not matched the barbell: a 260 kg deadlift that goes 3rd of 16 and a 171 kg clean and jerk are real, yet Weightlifting and Gymnastics both land in the teens percentile on the floor. The model has him 18th. Four Games trips say he belongs, but he needs the tests to reward the lifts directly rather than bury them inside skill and volume.
narratives.chris-ibarra: Ibarra is steady to a fault: an 81 consistency, the highest kind of mid-pack reliability, with Metabolic at the 66th percentile his best lane off a 5th in the 2025 Hammer Down. Nothing is a true hole, but nothing is a weapon either, the barbell and gymnastics both hovering near the middle. The model has him 14th. He climbs by out-lasting the volatile athletes around him, not by winning events outright.
narratives.sven-geens: Geens is a 34-year-old rookie with one lane and two big holes: Bodyweight at the 62nd percentile is fine, but sprint and heavy both at the 7th say anything fast or loaded ends his event early. The energy systems all read in the mid-30s, the profile of a grinder without a gear change. The model lands him 26th. He needs long, moderate, bodyweight-flavored tests, and even then the ceiling is modest.
narratives.fabian-hermans: Hermans is a technician without a tank: Balance, Coordination and Accuracy lead his skill read, but Bodyweight sits dead last in the field and every energy system reads near the bottom, for a 31.9 capacity and a 27th seed. A high 83.8 consistency just means he is reliably back. The control is real, the horsepower is not, so he needs a low-volume, skill-precise test to show anything.
narratives.tom-kingdon: Kingdon is an odd, lopsided rookie: best-in-field overhead squat, power clean and push jerk, and a 260 kg deadlift that goes 4th of 16, yet a back squat that lands 14th and a CHAD dead last. The model reads the whole as a 24th seed, with Metabolic his best domain at the 59th. The Olympic lifts are a genuine weapon; the grind and the engine are the questions. He needs barbell-technical tests, not long ones.
narratives.aniol-ekai: Ekai is power over patience: Heavy 72nd and Sprint 69th, with a 172 kg clean and jerk that goes 3rd of 16 to anchor the explosive end. The engine is the clear cost, Long Engine at the 14th percentile and a 19:10 5k that lands 6th of 8, so a long aerobic piece is where he drops out of the fight. One Games trip, 18th. The model has him 19th, and his path is short, heavy, and fast.
narratives.lucy-campbell: Campbell owns the apparatus: 100th-percentile gymnastics and 83rd bodyweight, the profile of an athlete who beats the entire field when the test goes upside down or high-skill. The barbell is the relative soft spot, Heavy 55th with a 135 kg squat that sits 7th of 9 and a 94 kg clean and jerk 9th of 10, so a heavy day is where the gap narrows. The model has her 2nd, and a 2nd-place Games finish says the ceiling is the podium. Keep it gymnastic and she wins.
narratives.mirjam-von-rohr: Von Rohr tops the women's model, and the engine is the reason: 100th-percentile Long Engine, a 92.2 phosphagen read, and energy systems that stay high across the board, so nothing falls out from under her. Her softest rooms, Sprint and Heavy, still sit 76th to 83rd, which means there is no real hole to exploit. One Games trip and a 7th already on the card. The number one seed is built on range, not a single trick.
narratives.emma-lawson: The file reads like a metronome: #4 of 30 projected on an 82 consistency. The metabolic engine is the separator at the 93rd percentile, backed by a 1st-place ride at the 2023 Ride, and the energy systems sit flat and high at 71.2, 72 and 74, so nothing drops out from under her. Even her softest domains stay elite, Heavy at the 86th and Weightlifting at the 93rd, with a 315 lb back squat that goes 3rd of 9 and a 240 lb clean and jerk 2nd of 10 to back it; the lone soft number is the 345 lb deadlift, 8th of 11.
narratives.leah-st-ren: Storen is the rookie nobody wants to draw: Heavy and Sprint both at the 100th percentile, a 91 consistency that is the highest in the field, and a benchmark card that is absurd, best-in-field bar muscle-ups, toes-to-bar and 5k plus a 365 lb deadlift. The model still flags low confidence because there is no Games tape, and her softest domains, oddly, are the long engine and gymnastics, both still in the 90s. A 7th seed that could be a lot higher.
narratives.var-thurmann-moe: Thurmann-Moe is a powerful rookie: Bodyweight at the 97th percentile and Heavy at the 90th, with Speed, Power and Strength leading her skill read off a strong barbell showing in QF Test 3. The relative softness is the apparatus and the long grind, both still in the 70s, so she is exposed more by high-skill gymnastics than by anything fast or heavy. The model has her 12th on a low-confidence band. A real threat if the tests stay explosive.
narratives.morgane-thyssens: Thyssens is a barbell rookie with elite numbers: best-in-field clean and jerk, front squat, overhead squat and bench, with Heavy and Sprint both at the 97th percentile and a 91.6 consistency. The tell is the gymnastics-engine side, a 2:33 Fran and 50 pull-ups that both land dead last, so a high-skill or high-volume bodyweight test is the hole. The model has her 11th. Loaded and short she is a threat; long and gymnastic she is exposed.
narratives.claudia-gluck: Gluck is quick and slick: Sprint 79th and Gymnastics 76th, the profile of an athlete who scores on fast, technical work, with a 1st in Open 26.2 to anchor it. The endurance side is the trade, Stamina and Endurance her softest skills and a Long Engine that fades to the middle, so a long grind is where she gives ground. The model has her 3rd. On a fast, skill-heavy floor she is a podium threat; on a marathon day she slides.
narratives.aline-wirz: Wirz is a 32-year-old rookie with a power lean: Heavy 66th and Bodyweight 59th, with Strength, Power and Speed topping her skill read. Nothing is a true weapon and nothing is a hole, the whole profile clustered just below the middle for a 56.2 capacity. The model has her 21st on a low-confidence band. She needs short, loaded tests to climb, because there is no engine or gymnastics edge to lean on when the work runs long.
narratives.elena-carratala: Projected 13th of 30, but the file hides a real tool: a 400m run of 1:00, best in the field, so any short sprint window is live. The barbell splits, a 90 kg squat snatch goes 4th of 11, yet Heavy sits at her 10th percentile and Grace at 1:50 is the softer mark, so loaded grinders pull her back. Long oxidative work, where she beats just 37 percent of the field, is the ceiling.
narratives.carolyne-prevost: Prevost is the field's grizzled grinder, 36 years old with a benchmark card that travels: best-in-field CHAD and Fight Gone Bad, plus a 330 lb squat and a 405 lb deadlift both 2nd in the field. On the floor the engine and the strength carry her, while gymnastics and bodyweight are the softer rooms. A high 80.9 consistency is the veteran tell. The model has her 9th, and she climbs by never blowing an event, not by winning one outright.
narratives.kyra-milligan: Milligan is all barbell: Heavy at the 93rd percentile and Weightlifting at the 83rd, with a 1st in QF Test 3 to prove the loaded work is the weapon. The flip side is volatile, a 66.6 consistency that is among the lowest up front and a bodyweight read at the 7th percentile, so a high-skill or high-volume gymnastics test can sink an event. The model still likes her 5th. Heavy days are where she wins; the swingy floor is the risk.
narratives.tayla-howe: Howe is a rookie with a clean two-lane profile: Bodyweight at the 93rd percentile and Heavy at the 79th, with Speed, Stamina and Power leading the skill read. The softer rooms are the long engine and gymnastics, both still mid-pack, so she is more exposed by technical apparatus than by anything fast. The model has her 18th on a low-confidence band. No Games tape, but the season says she can climb if the tests reward power and bodyweight strength.
narratives.rebecca-fuselier: Fuselier is a gymnastics specialist with a thin barbell: a best-in-field 1:59 Fran and 86 pull-ups say the bodyweight engine is genuinely fast, but a 285 lb squat that goes 8th of 9 and Heavy at the 17th percentile say the loaded work is the hole. The model has her 14th. Give her a high-skill, high-rep bodyweight test and she is live; put a barbell that climbs in front of her and the field pulls away.
narratives.aimee-cringle: Cringle is an engine athlete who can move load when she has to: Metabolic at the 79th percentile and a best-in-field 185 kg deadlift, with a 2nd in the 2025 Run/Row/Run to anchor the aerobic read. The relative softness is the technical barbell, Weightlifting and Heavy both around the 59th, still respectable. The model has her 6th. On a long, mixed floor she is a podium threat; she just needs the lifting to stay simple rather than skillful.
narratives.olivia-geisthardt: Geisthardt is a one-note rookie: Bodyweight at the 86th percentile is genuinely good, with a 6th in Open 26.1 behind it, but metabolic and sprint both sit at the floor and the energy systems read in the 20s, for a 29.5 capacity and a 29th seed. The single tool is real; the tank and the speed are not there yet. She needs a pure bodyweight test to register, and even then the weekend is steep.
narratives.maddi-foutz: Foutz is a rookie with a faint power lean and not much separation: Heavy and Sprint her best at the low-30s percentile, the whole profile sitting below the field for a 44.8 capacity. A high 85.8 consistency means she is reliably mid-to-back rather than volatile. The model has her 25th. There is no weapon to build a weekend around, so she needs the short, loaded tests to fall her way and a clean, error-free three days.
narratives.paige-rodgers: Rodgers is fast and agile: Gymnastics 66th and Sprint 59th, with Agility, Balance and Speed leading her skill read off a 3rd in the 2023 Inverted Medley. The barbell and the long grind are the softer rooms, Heavy 38th and a fading endurance read, so a heavy or marathon test is where she gives ground. The model has her 16th. Her path up is short and gymnastic; her risk is anything that gets heavy or long.
narratives.bergros-bjornsdottir: Bjornsdottir is 19 and already owns one elite tool: Bodyweight at the 100th percentile, top of the entire field, with a 3rd in Open 26.1 and a 1st in QF Test 1 to back the engine. The barbell is the young athlete's gap, Sprint and Heavy both in the low 30s, so a heavy day exposes her. The model has her 22nd on a low-confidence band. The ceiling is high; the strength just has to catch up to the gymnastics.
narratives.siria-meha: Meha is a strength athlete in a field that punishes one-dimensional profiles: Heavy and Weightlifting her best, with Strength, Power and Accuracy topping the skill read, but bodyweight and metabolic both at the 10th percentile and a 34.5 capacity. The model has her 17th. The barbell can win her a single event, but the engine and the gymnastics are where the field opens a gap she cannot close over three days.
narratives.ella-wilkinson: Wilkinson is the steadiest unknown in the field: a 95.7 consistency, the highest of anyone, with Heavy and Sprint her best lanes in the mid-40s percentile. The flip side is that nothing spikes, the whole profile clustered near the middle for a 47.6 capacity. The model has her 24th on a low-confidence band. She will not blow events, but without a weapon she needs the field around her to make the mistakes she does not.
narratives.afroditi-grigoriadi: Grigoriadi is a volatile rookie: a 1st in Open 26.3 says the gymnastics ceiling is real, but a bodyweight read at the floor, a 66.1 consistency that is among the lowest in the field, and a 44.3 capacity say the bottom can fall out fast. The model has her 26th. She can win a high-skill event outright, then give it all back on the next piece, an event-stealer more than a contender.
narratives.anikha-greer: Greer is a pure sprinter: an 81.3 phosphagen read and Sprint at the 62nd percentile, with a 2nd in the 2025 back-squat test showing the short, explosive end is the weapon. The engine is the opposite extreme, Long Engine at the 0th percentile and oxidative work where the field simply leaves her. One Games trip and a 9th already. The model has her 20th, and her whole weekend hinges on the tests staying short, because anything long is a write-off.
narratives.grace-walton: Walton is a balanced engine athlete: Metabolic 66th and Bodyweight 52nd, with Stamina, Endurance and Speed leading the skill read off a 1st in the 2024 Firestorm. Nothing is a glaring hole, with gymnastics and sprint just below the middle, so she is more solid than spiky. The model has her 10th. She climbs by stacking steady finishes on the mixed-modal work rather than winning the specialist tests outright.
narratives.danielle-brandon: Brandon is fast and explosive: Sprint at the 90th percentile, a best-in-field 210 lb snatch and a 240 lb clean and jerk that goes 3rd of 10, the profile of an athlete who scores on short, athletic, high-skill work. The long grind and the heavy barbell are the softer rooms, both still in the 70s, so a marathon piece is where she gives a little. Seven Games deep with a 4th best, the model has her 8th, and on a fast, gymnastic floor she is a podium threat.
narratives.laura-plaza-gonzalez: Plaza Gonzalez is a bodyweight-only rookie: a 66th-percentile bodyweight read with a 9th in Open 26.1, but metabolic and sprint both near the floor and the energy systems all in the mid-30s, for a 36.7 capacity. Balance and Stamina lead the skill read, which fits; the engine and the speed do not. The model has her 28th. She needs a calm, gymnastic test to show anything; a fast or heavy floor ends her event early.
narratives.hattie-kanyo: Kanyo is a 34-year-old with a power lean and a real engine gap: a 200 lb squat snatch that goes 3rd of 11, with Speed and Power topping the skill read, but Long Engine at the 7th percentile and Gymnastics at the 14th. Two Games trips say she belongs, the model has her 27th. The short, loaded work is where she scores; anything long or high-skill is where the field, and the years, catch up.
narratives.lydia-fish: Fish is a young strength athlete with a familiar gap: Heavy at the 69th percentile and Strength and Power leading the skill read off a 2nd in the 2025 Climbing Couplet, but a bodyweight read at the 24th and a phosphagen of 22.3 that says the very top-end speed is missing. One Games trip, 13th. The model has her 15th. She wins on loaded, controlled tests; she is exposed when the work goes light, fast, and high-skill.
narratives.miley-wade: Wade is 18 and the youngest in the field, and the numbers read like a debut: a 30th seed at 26.7 capacity, with gymnastics and the long engine her best at the 3rd percentile and the energy systems all in the mid-20s. Balance and Coordination lead the skill read, the raw material of a future contender. The model has her last for now. This is a learning weekend, with the ceiling years away rather than this July.
narratives.jennifer-muir: Muir is a sprinter with a single big hole: a 77.9 phosphagen read and Power and Strength leading the skill list, but Gymnastics at the 0th percentile, the kind of gap the Games will find. One trip, a 20th. The model has her 23rd. She can flash on a short, explosive test, but a high-skill apparatus piece is an event she effectively gives away, and there are too many of those across three days.
narratives.haley-adams: Adams is a pure engine: Metabolic at the 97th percentile and Bodyweight at the 90th, the profile of an athlete who beats the field on mixed-modal and gymnastic volume. The barbell is the honest weakness, a 255 lb squat and a 205 lb clean and jerk both dead last in the field, so a heavy day is where she leaks real points. Six Games deep with a 4th best, the model has her 19th, lower than the engine suggests because the loaded tests cost her.
